reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: DeGray Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Randy Plyler with Plyler Outdoors Guide Service (870-210-0522) said that with water temps in the low to mid-50s, bass can be caught on Alabama rigs or shaky head minnow by looking at your LiveScope and look for balls of baitfish. Also, bass can be caught on lipless crankbaits and crankbaits running to 12 feet deep along the moss and close to ledges.
Crappie can be caught on minnows and jigs in 15-25 feet on brush and standing timber.
Just two weeks ago there was a whopping 14.2-pound largemouth bass caught out here using a shaky head minnow by LiveScoping.”

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Maumelle fishing report
reports.text:
Black bass are fair. Largemouths are reportedly being caught deep to 15-20 feet. Jigs, an Alabama rig and crankbaits are recommended. Spotted bass (aka Kentucky bass) are mixed in with the largemouths in 15-20 feet. Drop-shot, Carolina rigs, jigs and cranks seem to work best.
Crappie are fair, though some anglers said they were having good results. Some reports have them roaming around the channel, and they can be found off of brushpiles anywhere from 20-30 feet deep. Try jigs and minnows.

A lot of big fish are coming in right now, stripers for a lot of people spooning on stripers, as well as white bass, and some are catching largemouths and Kentucky bass (spots) in with them.
“Crappie have been really good, with some monster crappie.

reports.text: * We’re not seeing as much random schooling largemouth bass over the past week with the cold fronts dropping lake surface temps, and we’re not seeing as much surface breaking as last week. reports.text:
Fish ’N Stuff (501-834-5733) says the black bass have moved up a little bit more shallow of late.
Crappie on the river are doing pretty good, they report. They’re in 10-12 feet of water on brushpiles or off the ends of jetties. Best success, they’re hearing, is by throwing a one-sixteenth-ounce jighead (unpainted or pink) with a black and chartreuse jig.

reports.text:
Melanie Fitzgibbon at Cane Creek State Park (870-628-4714) said the biggest action recently was one angler buying a quarter-pound of minnows “to try his theory of fishing in the rain for crappie by boat” last Saturday.
Most of the best fishing the past month has been for crappie out on the lake via boat, though the interior dock has been a fair spot for catfish.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Greers Ferry Lake fishing report
reports.text:
For crappie, try super shallow and out to 30 feet using jigs, minnows or crankbaits.
Black bass are found in singles shallow, but most groups are out in the lake roaming shallow and schooling.
(updated 12-19-2024) Fish ’N Stuff (501-834-5733) in Sherwood said Thursday that the smallmouth bass are doing really well in 15-20 feet of water. The largemouths and spotted bass are doing well off main lake points.
Crappie on the lake are doing pretty good as well. They are being caught in 20-25 feet of water, and an eighth-ounce jighead (try silver or pink) with a black and chartreuse body is your best ticket to success.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Harris Brake Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Harris Brake Lake Resort (501-889-2745) says that the crappie have been doing well lately and anglers have caught some big slabs — some 15-15.5 inches in length and up to 2 pounds — fishing from the shoreline. Other nice crappie have been hauled in by anglers using boats. Water around the shoreline is only about 2 feet in depth where the close-in crappie are biting.
Crappie are also being caught in good numbers on the other side of the lake from the resort, they hear.
The best time for the crappie and white bass bite has been from about 5:30 a.m. to 8 a.m.

Also, the smallmouth are being found on deep rockpiles in 20 feet of water, with a Carolina rig or a football jig being your best bet.
Crappie slowed some with the cold front but they’ve been biting in about 15 feet of water.
While the cold front may have slowed the crappie activity, the walleye are beginning to pick up.
Crappie continue to be found super shallow out to 30 feet.
As for black bass, the loners are shallow, but most are out or roaming shallow and schooling.

reports.text: Shelly Jeffrey at Lake Charles State Park (870-878-6595) said black bass and catfish were the most active this past week at Lake Charles, but even that action was fair. reports.text: Harris Brake Lake Resort (501-889-2745) says decent-sized crappie have been caught, and overall crappie have been doing pretty well, including one 15-inch catch and one that weighed in at almost 2.5 pounds. The angler catching the heaviest crappie was using a jig while the woman who caught the 15-inch crappie was using minnow. Large numbers of crappie have been caught, too, early in the morning and early at night (7 p.m. or so). Anglers fishing from a boat toward the shoreline also said they caught decent-sized crappie.

reports.text: The largemouth bass bite is good. There are reports of the bass around the edges of channels following baitfish. Use jigs, Alabama rigs, swimbaits, and try jerk baits in shallow water in the afternoon. Look for bass around isolated structures looking for bream and shad around 18 feet of water. For crappie fish, best success is going to come fishing in 10-12 feet of water away from the shoreline with minnows or jigs.

reports.text: Philip Kastner of Trader Bill’s Outdoors in Little Rock and Hot Springs said on the weekly “Wild Side Show” on KABZ-FM, 103.7 The Buzz that Lake Hamilton is now drawn down 5 feet and that’s made it perfect for crappie fishing. If you’ve got brush piles with 8-10 feet of water over the top of the pile, that’s exactly where all the crappie are on this lake. Hamilton has bass tournament after bass tournament out here every single weekend. But all of the crappie fishermen are laughing while they’re stocking the deep freezer because there is fish to be caught every day.”

reports.text: Largemouth bass fishing is good. Some reports have the bass being found still scattered at all depths, but most are deep. Kentucky bass ( spotted bass ) are fair. reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millwood Lake fishing report
reports.text: * Largemouth bass reactions slowed over the past week. The black bass are continually roaming and following the huge pods of threadfin shad in the oxbows along Little River and in mouths of the creeks that dump into the river. Shad have been randomly surface-breaking when the bass are pushing the huge schools and pods of shad to surface. Bass will continue to be roaming with the cooler water temperatures, following the shad schools on primary and secondary points and into the creek channels. “We found several schools of 2- to 4-pound largemouths staging on points, and a few decent bass were already deep into the creek channels where the shad began moving into the backs of several creeks…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Norfork Lake fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass fishing has also been very good for me. The fish I am finding and catching are in 30 to maybe 36 feet of water relating to underwater points, small drop-offs, small humps or to nearby brush piles. The areas that I have found to be the best are typically out in the middle of the lake. Small schools are feeding at different times of day. When you find these feeding fish it has been very normal to land 5 to 10 nice size largemouth in a very short period of time. Just remember when you jig up a bass and are reeling it up to the boat do not let the fish jump out of the water. If they do get to jump 9 times out of 10 you have lost the fish. You can also find bass in tighter to…

reports.text: Bass up to this point have been very good. Now that the cold wave of high pressure has moved in for a few days, the fishing has really dropped off. reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Greers Ferry Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are stacked around pole timber and piles and getting more so every day. Black bass are still from super shallow out to 60 feet eating a variety of baits.
(updated 12-3-2020) Fish ’N Stuff (501-834-5733) in Sherwood says smallmouth bass are biting well on Alabama rigs, jerkbaits and Rat-L-Traps on main lake points and along creeks.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Harris Brake Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good, though. Best fishing for crappie is around the shoreline. Also, crappie are biting trotlines with minnows. Black bass are good; look in the deeper areas of the lake.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Dardanelle fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing has been really good. Crappie have been very good in 8 foot of water; mayfly has the colour of the week.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayetteville fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing is fair; uses minnows or jigs. Black bass are biting fair on plastic worms and topwater baits.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Monticello fishing report
reports.text: * Largemouth bass: The water temperatures continue dropping a few degrees overnight with the incoming cold fronts, ranging upper 40s to mid-50 range. The Millwood Mayhem continues with the largemouth and white bass feeding and schooling at random in many locations near/over vertical structure in timber. Numerous schools and pods of bass continue chasing shad in Horseshoe, McGuire and Mud oxbows up Little River the past couple weeks, with the best period of feeding early to midafternoon. Heavy, ¾-ounce 1-knocker Rat-L-Traps in Millwood Magic, Transparent Holographic Shad and Splatterback Shad continue working subsurface when the bass are chasing and busting the shad near standing timber in…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nimrod fishing report
reports.text: Crappie reports have been good. Crappie are found in 5-6 feet depth and are biting red/chartreuse jigs, black/chartreuse jigs and Beaver Bottom Jigs. Black bass are good; find them in shallow water hitting spinnerbaits and crankbaits.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Overcup fishing report
reports.text:
Randy DeHart at Lakeview Landing (501-354-5309) said the cold weather has pushed the crappie into shallower water and anglers are catching quite a few keepers right now. Crappie are good on small minnows and on jigs; he says pink, white and chartreuse are the good colors.
Black bass have been doing well and chasing shad.
He adds that crappie are doing well off the docks on the 95 side, but have been slow the last couple of days.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sequoyah fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are good, with small crankbaits working best. The bite for black bass is slow, while catfishing is very slow.
(updated 12-3-2020) Shelly Jeffrey at Lake Charles State Park (870-878-6595) said crappie continue to bite well while the bass bite is fair. Minnows or a black/chartreuse jig will work for the good crappie bite. Black bass are favoring shaky head jigs.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Little Maumelle River fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on minnows and jigs. Black bass are good using crankbaits or plastic worms.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Bear Creek Lake/Storm Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Tyler Ball, park ranger at Mississippi River State Park (870-295-4040), says anglers have had success catching crappie from depths of 12-15 feet due to cooler weather. Anglers have reported catching crappie on minnows and jigs.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Beaverfork fishing report
reports.text: Crappie have been found midway down and the bite is excellent. Black bass are roaming all over and all depths and, like crappie, the bite is excellent.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ouachita fishing report
reports.text:
Todd Gadberry at Mountain Harbor Resort and Spa (870-867-2191/800-832-2276 out of state) reports that black bass are fair. Spotted bass (Kentucky bass) are still schooled up chasing baitfish. Crappie are still good.
(updated 11-25-2020) John Koestler at Masterbaiters Bait and Tackle (501-209-6538) on Arkansas Highway 7 reports that the fishing in Lake Ouachita was rough, but they did manage to get some bass on crankbaits and also jigging spoons. Crappie bite should be good in a week or two. Points have also been producing walleye and bass.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Atkins fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing is good. There were no reports on bream, bass or catfish.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Dardanelle fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing has been really good. Crappie have been very good in 8 foot of water; mayfly has the color of the week.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River fishing report
reports.text: Zimmerman’s Exxon (501-944-2527) reports that crappie are being caught in good numbers on jigs, specifically a Bobby Garland Cajun Cricket.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are good behind the jetties at 8-10 feet depth. Black bass are fair and are hitting crankbaits.
(updated 12-18-2019) Zimmerman’s Exxon (501-944-2527) reports that crappie are good in Wood Oak Bayou in Burns Park. They’re in 4-5 feet depth and are hitting Popeye jigs (chartreuse Crappie Magnet). Below Terry Lock and Dam, it’s much the same, with crappie good in 4-5 feet depth of water around the Willow Bend area. No reports on bass.
(updated 12-18-2019) McSwain Sports Center (501-945-2471), reporting on the fishing near the Terry Lock and Dam, said that black bass are fair on crankbaits and worms. Bream and crappie are poor.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Bishop Park Ponds fishing report
reports.text: Lisa Spencer at Lisa’s Bait Shop (501-778-6944) said some small crappie and bass have been coming from both ponds this week.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Bull Shoals Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair. Black bass are fair.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Clear Lake fishing report
reports.text: The crappie bite is fair on minnows or jigs. Black bass are fair on crankbaits and worms.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Greers Ferry Lake fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are eating a long list of baits if you get it in front of one. Crappie are eating it up as well.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Harris Brake Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in deep water and the bite is good. Minnows and jigs are working along with other lures and crappie minnows.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Atkins fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good. Bass reports are poor.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fort Smith fishing report
reports.text: I dug around Facebook and found that one of the locals caught a monster bass on a crankbait a few days ago, but I cannot confirm the body of water that he was fishing on.”

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Hamilton fishing report
reports.text:
Bass over the last week were good, before the weather pushed through, on Damiki rigs in shad colors and drop-shot rigs with green pumpkin worms in the guts of creek channels and ditches in between main lake points.
Crappie continue to pick up, and when the water temps get to 45 degrees they should be filling coolers and live wells.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Norrell fishing report
reports.text: Lisa Spencer at Lisa’s Bait Shop (501-778-6944) said crappie are still biting size 6 minnows and some jigs for a few customers. They report catching nice-sized crappie but no big numbers and actually catching and releasing more bass than crappie.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ouachita fishing report
reports.text: Todd Gadberry at Mountain Harbor Resort and Spa (870-867-2191/800-832-2276 out of state) reports that black bass are fair to good. Crappie are fair.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Winona fishing report
reports.text: Lisa Spencer at Lisa’s Bait Shop (501-778-6944) said she’s heard no recent reports from Winona, but some customers have been headed that way with a mix of size 6 and size 12 minnows in search of crappie.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Little Maumelle River fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are have made a good turnaround in the last few days, Ray said Monday, and anglers report good catches using minnows and jigs. Bass are fair on crankbaits and soft plastic worms.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millwood Lake fishing report
reports.text: Mike says the cooler weather over the past couple weeks has all but eliminated the surface-breaking fish, and the largemouth bass and Kentucky bass are randomly feeding deeper and slower, yet still following the threadfin shad schools. Bass have moved out of lily pad stands to vertical structure on deeper drops into the oxbows and into the 9-12 feet depth range, and continue following huge schools of shad. The largemouths, Kentuckys and white bass are following these schools of shad, and the whites have been the most aggressive over the past week couple weeks. Square-bill crankbaits, Rat-L-Traps and Fat Free Fry, and Fat Free Guppy continue randomly connecting with the bunched-up bass…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Saline River Access in Benton fishing report
reports.text: Smallmouth and Kentucky bass were biting fair on brooder minnows but the walleye were slow to bite anything. Crappie have been biting fair on minnows fished around brush or logs in deeper water.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Spring River fishing report
reports.text: Guppies and White Lightnings are working well for the bass – smallmouth and largemouth.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Sunset Lake fishing report
reports.text: Lisa Spencer at Lisa’s Bait Shop (501-778-6944) said crappie fishing has been fair for a few customers using No. We’ve had no reports of bass or bream being caught recently.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Walcott Lake fishing report
reports.text: Last week, anglers did catch a few bass.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Brewer Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good. A lot of crappie are being caught about 2-3 feet from brushpiles or by the creek bed coming into the lake. Bass are fair, with the best activity coming during the evening.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sequoyah fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair. Largemouth bass are good.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Beaver Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Fishing has been pretty good for all of the big three species on Beaver: stripers, bass and crappie. Bass are good in brushpiles in 20-30 feet depth and main lake points and rock humps. “I have caught numerous spots and blacks while fishing for crappie in those exact areas. Crappie were doing real well but the last two days it has really become difficult. Look for crappie school up on brush and treetops in 15-35 feet of water.
Crappie are good. Black bass are good mostly on Wiggle Warts or other crankbaits.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Buffalo National River/Crooked Creek fishing report
reports.text: The smallmouths are much less active in the cold weather.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good both early in the morning and late in the day on minnows and jigs. Bass are good on crankbaits.
reports.lake: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good and are biting at 8-10 feet depth.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are biting at 10 feet depth and the results have been good. Black/chartreuse or pink/chartreuse crappie jigs are your best bet. Black bass are good and are being caught in 5-10 feet depth of water. Moving into the backwater grassy or rocky areas, bass will be attracted to white/green pumpkin chatterbaits.
(updated 12-11-2019) Zimmerman’s Exxon (501-944-2527) reports that fishing is pretty much the same as it was last week, with crappie being fair. Black bass are fair; best bet is to use a shad-colored Rat-L-Trap. Sauger are being caught on black/pink crappie jigs below the Murray dam.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Beaver Lake fishing report
reports.text:
I was catching crappie mixed in with the white bass suspended in 5-10 feet of water under shad balls. This time of the year crappie follow the bait and do not have to be on structure whatsoever. I found some massive schools of crappie in Blue Springs last Monday and Tuesday.
Bass have been pretty good on clear end – spotted bass are schooled up off main points. I promise you Garmin Panoptix Livescope is a game changer and is a ton of fun catching crappie and walleye with it.”
Crappie are good on minnows and jigs.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Bishop Park Ponds fishing report
reports.text: Lisa Spencer at Lisa’s Bait Shop (501-778-6944) said catfish fair on bass minnows and cut up skipjack and small frozen shad. Bass are good on brooder minnows and crankbaits. Crappie good on pink minnows and No. 6 crappie minnows.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Bull Shoals Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good, but their running deep. Crappie are good and are found around the shad.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Clear Lake fishing report
reports.text: The crappie bite has been good for a while now, with nightcrawlers, minnows and jigs all working. Black bass are good on minnows.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Greers Ferry Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are eating steady in 15-40 feet of water on minnows, jigs, trolled crankbaits or slow-reeling a Road Runner. Bass fishing is good top to bottom on a variety of baits, moving or drug along bottom.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Harris Brake Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on minnows or Bobby Garland pink and blue jigs. Poor reports on bream, bass and catfish.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Atkins fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on minnows and jigs. Black bass are fair.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Hamilton fishing report
reports.text:
Largemouth and spotted Bass are doing quite well when found. Most of the bass can be found in the gut or just inside main lake point tributaries. Crappie are fair to good at depths of 20-35 feet of treetops and brushpiles.
Darryl Morris at Family Fishing Trips said the crappie are moving into their winter patterns on cover where there is deep water nearby. Crappie have been harvested on both jigs and minnows fished 12 feet and as deep as 20 feet.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Norrell fishing report
reports.text: Lisa Spencer at Lisa’s Bait Shop (501-778-6944) said crappie have been big but not big in quantities. 6 crappie minnows, some Kalin’s Bleeding Tennessee Shad-colored 2-inch grubs. Bass are fair on brooder minnows and plastic worms.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sequoyah fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair using tube jigs. Black bass are good on crankbaits, plastic worms. Smallmouth bass are being caught on Red Rigs (first time in a decade, they report).

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Winona fishing report
reports.text: Lisa Spencer at Lisa’s Bait Shop (501-778-6944) said crappie are good on bass minnows and blue and silver grubs. Catfish are good on bait shrimp, bass minnows and nightcrawlers. Bass are good on minnows.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millwood Lake fishing report
reports.text: Cooler weather this week has tapered off the surface schooling/breaking fish, but the largemouth bass and Kentucky bass continue feeding deeper and slower, following the threadfin shad schools with only random surface-breaking this week. Bass have moved out of lily pad stands to vertical structure on deeper drops into the oxbows and into 9-12 feet depth, and continue following huge schools of shad. The largemouths, spotted bass and white bass are following these schools of shad, and the whites have been the most aggressive over the past week. Square-bill crankbaits like the Echo 1.75 in shad patterns and Ghost Minnow, Rat-L-Traps and Bomber Fat Free Fry, Shad and Fat Free Guppy continue…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Saline River Access in Benton fishing report
reports.text:
Brooder minnows are what he caught them on along with several nice smallmouth and Kentucky bass.
Lisa says she hasn’t heard any reports of crappie on the Saline River or at least not around these parts of it, which the Saline goes a good ways.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Sunset Lake fishing report
reports.text: Lisa Spencer at Lisa’s Bait Shop (501-778-6944) said a few catfish are being caught off of bass minnows and nightcrawlers. Bass are good off of brooder minnows and crankbaits. Crappie are good on pink crappie minnows fishing deep and some along with crappie nibbles.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Walcott Lake fishing report
reports.text: Walcott Lake (Crowley’s Ridge State Park) reports anglers catching three nice bass over the weekend. They said the fishing were biting well and that they also missed several bass.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: White River fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair, though.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Felsenthal fishing report
reports.text: Sportsman’s One Stop in El Dorado (870-863-7248) said a lot of bass and crappie are being caught. Bass are biting well on crankbaits, spinnerbaits and soft plastics. Crappie can be caught on jigs and shiners in the river and old river bed. Crappie fisherman are catching some nice bream, also.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Horseshoe Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie also are excellent. Ronnie reports catching about 40 crappie on a busy Tuesday. Crappie are in shallow water and around brushpiles. Black bass are poor, no reports.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nimrod fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good and being caught at 10-12 feet depth in the river on minnows and jigs. Black bass are good, with best results on jigs or black and blue frogs.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on minnows and jigs. Black bass are good on spinnerbaits and crankbaits.
reports.lake: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River fishing report
reports.text:
Fishing is still going well for crappie or bass, though. Crappie are being found at a depth of 5-10 feet and are being caught at the rocky points, ends of jetties on black/blue jigs, chrome/black Rat-L-Traps and blue/white or blue/chartreuse crappie jigs. Black bass are being caught using black crankbaits or Rat-L-Traps; they’re also best around the rocky points.
(updated 12-4-2019) Zimmerman’s Exxon (501-944-2527) reports that crappie are fair. Black bass are fair; best bet is to use a shad-colored Rat-L-Trap. Sauger are being caught on black/pink crappie jigs below the Murray dam. You’ll find sauger eager to bite too on black/pink crappie jigs.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Beaver Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are around structure in 15-20 feet water. Piney Creek is holding crappie. Black bass are hit or miss on various baits.
Crappie are biting well, mostly around cover, brushpiles and rocky points.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Bull Shoals Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are found about 20 feet depth and the bite is good; fish around the brushpiles. Black bass are fair on plastic worms.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Clear Lake fishing report
reports.text: The crappie bite continues to be good, with minnows and jigs working. Black bass fell off with the high water, though; poor results.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Harris Brake Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good. Some anglers are limiting on crappie. Black bass are fair and are biting goldfish or bass minnows.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Horseshoe Lake fishing report
reports.text: Ronnie is using waxworms, crickets and crappie jigs. Crappie are good. There are crappie in the 2-pound range that are deep and being caught trolling. No reports lately on black bass, he said.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Atkins fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on minnows and jigs. Black bass reports have been poor for a while.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nimrod fishing report
reports.text: Crappie were doing well until the water jumped up, they report. Poor reports across the board on bream, black bass, catfish and white bass.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millwood Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Mike says the largemouth and spotted bass bite has tapered off somewhat this week, but the white bass activity is still heavy. They are catching over 20 white bass a day still, where now they may only catch 3-4 black bass, he said.
Square-bill crankbaits like the Echo 1.75 in shad patterns and Ghost Minnow, Rat-L-Traps and Bomber Fat Free Fry, Shad and Fat Free Guppy continue catching these schooled-up bass.
The crappie in the river have scattered over the past couple weeks with the increased current and muddy inflow in Little River, but in the back of the oxbow lakes along Little River the crappie are recovering and biting jigs and minnows near standing timber where water clarity is much…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Norfork Lake fishing report
reports.text:
One of our meals during the week was a Norfork Lake Crappie fish fry, and, boy, was it good.”
Today I landed walleye and crappie on the spoon. Other days largemouth bass have been plentiful.
“In general, crappie are still hanging in the brush on the tops of the brush. Don’t hesitate to check out some very shallow brush on these sunny days, the crappie may move up.
“Bass fishing has basically stayed the same as my last report. As you know I like to find the deep bass.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Little Maumelle River fishing report
reports.text: Anglers are catching just a few bream while they’re crappie fishing. The crappie are fair on minnows or jigs. Black bass are fair on soft plastic worms or on crankbaits.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cane Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: “The short warmup we had didn’t seem to harm to crappie fishing too much. Bass are in a cold-weather pattern that should stay until spring. The more commotion there is, the better you stir those sluggish bass into biting.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good using crappie minnows or jigs. Black bass are good on spinnerbaits and crankbaits.
reports.lake: Craig D. Campbell Lake Conway Reservoir

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River fishing report
reports.text: Zimmerman’s Exxon (501-944-2527) said crappie are excellent.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River fishing report
reports.text:
Zimmerman’s Exxon (501-944-2527) reported that crappie remain excellent in the river around the Burns Park area, in the backwater and near Cajun’s Wharf on the Little Rock side. Use jigs, Shad Buster, crappie jigs in silver with a chartreuse tail. Bass are fair in the Little Rock pool; go below Terry Lock and Dam for excellent bite bites; throw Super Flukes.
Bass reports have been good. No reports on bream, crappie or catfish, however.
Crappie are excellent. No reports on bass, catfish or bream.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River fishing report
reports.text: The University of Arkansas at Pine Bluff Bass Fishing Team reports the water temperature is around 50 degrees and the water clarity is murky, less than 6 inches of visibility. The whole pool is quite dirty from the rainfall runoff lately and the black bass are lethargic.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Beaver Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie action continues to be good. Bass are fair and are hitting topwaters, crankbaits and big shad-looking jigs.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Bishop Park Ponds fishing report
reports.text: Lisa Spencer at Lisa’s Bait Shop (501-778-6944) said the pond in the back has been doing well on crappie using No. 6 crappie minnows. While they haven’t been very big crappie, anglers have been getting a good amount. 12 bass minnows and stink bait.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Brewer Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are excellent. Fish with minnows, chartreuse twister tails and with Crappie Magnet on the bottom. Bass are fair – “spotty,” Larry says – are are best around the brush with a crankbait.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Clear Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are excellent. No reports on bass, catfish or bream.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Greers Ferry Lake fishing report
reports.text: The crappie catching is good on jigs and minnows in the pole timber and in and around brush piles in the 12- to 30-foot range straight up and down, and that bite will be good all winter. Bass fishing is good shallow to 60 feet of water on a variety of baits; pick your choice and stick with it all over the lake or rivers.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Harris Brake Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are excellent. Bass are good. Anglers are have success with plastic worms, shiners and large bass minnows.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Atkins fishing report
reports.text:
Angler Bennie Goodman said crappie are really active in the coves at night. Bream, bass and catfish are poor.
Crappie are excellent, as has been the case the past few weeks. Bass are poor.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Dardanelle fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass has been slow due to the dirty water, but the best bite has been on dark jerkbaits, and plastic crawls, along with small jigs and Bamboozle. Crappie have been slow due to the dirty water and current. Bream have been caught on small jigs while crappie fishing in the creeks in 12 feet of water.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Greeson fishing report
reports.text: The bass are moving into their winter patterns. Crappie are really good lately.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Maumelle fishing report
reports.text:
Largemouth bass are good. With the water temperatures in the high 40s some bass are being caught in 10-15 feet near stumps, as well as some being found suspended off creek channels in 20-25 feet of water. Kentucky bass (spotted bass) are good. They are mixed in with the largemouth bass, but most can be found in 10-15 foot of water. Some whites are being caught on brush piles with the crappie in 20-30 feet of water. Crappie are great.
Crappie continue staging in their fall pattern.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nimrod fishing report
reports.text: Anglers reports poor results across the board: bream, crappie, bass, catfish and white bass.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Norrell fishing report
reports.text:

reports.title: Lake Ouachita fishing report
reports.text:
Spotted bass have been biting the shaky head jig on light leaders. Largemouth bass have been spotted laying up in the very shallow (less than a foot) in the mornings and acting very lethargic. Crappie is slow on the lake in 15-25 feet of water.
(updated 12-13-2017) Todd Gadberry at Mountain Harbor Resort and Spa (870-867-2191/800-832-2276 out of state) says black bass are fair. Crappie are fair and being caught on minnows in 20-30 feet of water near structure.

reports.title: War Eagle Creek fishing report
reports.text: Loy Lewis of War Eagle Creek Outfitting (479-530-3262) said smallmouth bass fishing good at times usually according to weather, the sunny afternoons be good time for sight fishing w spoons, and bluff holes have action w watermelon colored plastics….on the waterfowl report, the ducks are flying up river in the mornings regularly and with decoys they will land fast.

reports.title: Arkansas River fishing report
reports.text:
The crappie bite is fair, with jigs getting the best response. Bass reports were fair. Bass are biting spinnerbaits, crankbaits and Rat-L-Traps.
(update 11-29-2017) McSwain Sports Center (501-945-2471) said crappie are doing very well. Reports of nice catches of crappie off the river in the deeper water on minnows and jigs.
Crappie reports were good. Crappie are in 5-6 feet of water and are biting jigs as well as Fin Spin jigheads and curly jigs. No reports on bream, bass, catfish or white bass.

reports.title: DeGray Lake fishing report
reports.text:
He says that bass fishing should be good now because of the low water, which makes the fish bunch up more, but it’s been just the opposite, with the fish being really scarce. Crappie were good on the deeper attractors in October and early November.
Darryl Morris at Family Fishing Trips said crappie can still be caught in the 8- to 12-foot range but they are moving toward deeper wintertime waters.

reports.title: Millwood Lake fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass schooling activities have slightly diminished over the past couple of weeks. The random schooling on shad and the surfacing breaking over the past two weeks by largemouths and Kentuckies ( spotted bass ) have been totally awesome, but it slowed this week. Bass have been randomly schooling on flats in the lily pads, in creek channels adjacent to these same flats, and in Little River, surface breaking on the schools of shad during heat of the day. These bass have been very good from 2-3 pounds on topwaters, Rat-L-Traps, Bass Assassin Shads, Stuttersteps, and squarebill cranks. Bass Assassin Shads continue working well and best reaction Mike has had remains on the Grey Ghost…
